keyframe_review.note: New keyframe; Cliopatria has no row for the Bishopric of Dorpat (its Livonian Conference row of 1422-1561 covers Old Livonia as a whole, bishoprics included). The page says the bishopric 'generally covered the area that now comprises Tartu County, Põlva County, Võru County, and Jõgeva County'; no boundary or area. The page dates the bishopric to 1211 as the Bishopric of Leal, but the Dorpat land is drawn from 1224.

ledger.note: 1224: the bishopric takes Dorpat as its centre. 'The Sword Brothers captured Yuryev (modern Tartu) and renamed it Dorpat. Bishop Hermann then chose Dorpat as his centre'; Hermann von Buxhoeveden, brother of Albert of Riga, is bishop 1224-48. The page says the state 'was originally established as the Bishopric of Leal in 1211'; the page does not place Leal, so the Dorpat land is started at the page's 1224 date for Dorpat (confidence 2 on the start). The ancient-estonia dossier has Tartu falling to the Brothers in August 1224.

ledger.note: 1558: Russia conquers Tartu. 'In 1558 Tartu was conquered by Russian troops and the Bishopric of Dorpat ceased to exist.' The Livonian War page has 'Russian troops took Dorpat (Tartu) in May, Narva in July' and a footnote citing De Madariaga for Narva in May and Dorpat in July; May is used. Hermann Wesel (bishop 1552-60) is the last bishop listed.

wars.outcome: Russian troops took Dorpat in 1558 and the bishopric ceased to exist; the weakened Livonian Order was dissolved by the second Treaty of Vilnius in 1561.
wars.note: The Dorpat page also records the Battle on Lake Peipus of 1242, where Bishop Hermann and his Ugaunian subjects were defeated by Alexander Nevsky; no land changed hands on the page, and the page does not call it the Battle on the Ice.

certainty.note: The page names the four counties only; the Estonian county borders stand for the bishopric's boundary.

notes: The state is an ecclesiastical principality of Terra Mariana (Livonian Confederation member from 1435; the page does not mention the Confederation). Cliopatria's Livonian Conference polygon (1422-1561) covers Old Livonia with the bishoprics inside it; with this dossier the Confederation is an association and the Order's own shape should exclude the four counties. The Livonian Conference dossier files the 1558 loss of Dorpat under the Confederation. The bishopric's start is 1224, not the 1211 Leal date, because the page gives no location for the 1211 Bishopric of Leal and the first dated Dorpat sentence is 1224; the page states the territory as present-day counties, which is the researcher's reading for 1224-1558.
